title: Causal-Class Hierarchies in Coherence-Constrained Channel Transformation
authors: Lin Zhu, Benchi Zhao, Xuanqiang Zhao, Ranyiliu Chen, Xin Wang, Shenggen Zheng
abstract: Higher-order quantum transformations allow multiple channel uses to be combined through different causal architectures, from parallel and fixed-order sequential networks to general higher-order processes. Whether this causal freedom improves channel transformation when the higher-order operation is also constrained by a resource theory remains largely unexplored. We study this question in the dynamical resource theory of coherence using a unified semidefinite-programming framework. For two qubit amplitude-damping channels and the identity target, we prove a strict causal hierarchy at every nontrivial damping strength under both maximally incoherent superchannels (MISC) and dephasing-covariant incoherent superchannels (DISC). In contrast, mixed-Pauli channels admit a common teleportation simulation that transfers the channel dependence to Bell-diagonal program states prepared in parallel. The remaining processing can then be absorbed into a single quantum operational, so parallel, fixed-order sequential, and general higher-order strategies achieve the same optimal error for any target. These results identify free program-state parallelisation as a structural obstruction to causal enhancement.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes how the causal structure of multi-step quantum operations affects the efficiency of channel transformation under coherence constraints. Using SDPs, the authors prove that for some channels, the causal order matters significantly, while for others, the structure collapses, indicating that parallelization can negate any potential causal advantage.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether increasing causal freedom (from fixed-order sequential to general higher-order processes) improves quantum channel transformation when the process is constrained by a resource theory.
main_result: A strict causal hierarchy is proven for amplitude-damping channels, but this hierarchy collapses for mixed-Pauli channels, suggesting free program-state parallelization is a structural obstruction to causal enhancement.
method: The analysis employs a unified semidefinite-programming (SDP) framework to minimize the transformation error under various causal constraints (Parallel, Sequential, General) and coherence resource constraints (MISC, DISC).
model_or_system: The study models quantum channel transformations involving two resource channels and a target channel, focusing on two-qubit amplitude-damping channels and mixed-Pauli channels.
key_observables: The optimal error in channel transformation, $D_{	ext{Class}}^F(\dots)$, and the coherence coefficients ($x_c, \mu$).
important_parameters: The damping strength ($\epsilon$) of the amplitude-damping channels, and the specific coherence constraints (MISC or DISC).
main_assumptions: The collapse condition for causal enhancement is shown to be a sufficient, not necessary, characterization of structural obstructions.

paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the SDP framework, establishing the causal classes, deriving the necessary constraints for different orders, and finally applying these tools to prove the hierarchy for amplitude-damping channels and the collapse condition for mixed-Pauli channels.
why_interesting: The findings provide deep structural insights into the limitations of quantum operations, showing that the advantage of complex causal structures can be entirely nullified by the underlying resource properties of the channels involved.

Parallel protocols use both resource channels in one layer, while fixed-order sequential protocols connect the two calls through an intermediate memory. The class Gen denotes the general deterministic two-input higher-order feasible set used in this work; the schematic does not assert a particular circuit realization for an arbitrary element of Gen.
